Deddit is still strong, indeed. But alternatives are just a mouse click away. What they are doing is following what digg did, but with a few shrewd changes. And they actually might not even be aware of it. But they are banking on a new fresh user base that is either 1.) totally new to the web 2.) unaware of reddit 3.) aware of reddit but don't go there much. They are attempting to scrub the site of offending subs, certainly. What will be left are subs that are non-polarizing in nature and inspire dialogue that avoids political or social implications. The subs that remain will be hobby based (woodworking, pottery, gaming etc.) And even these hobby-based subs can be monetized. Then slowly, ever so slowly, bigger companies will infiltrate and steer the posts. If they are smart, they will do this really slowly so as to give the illusion of a lack of bias. To the untrained eye it will look great. Wow! What is this site? It's like...a.....collection of headllines. They will have discovered their first news aggregator site and think they hit the jackpot. The site will be almost fully monetized. The lure of this type of business plan is just too appealing. Indeed, there is a LOT of money to be made. The employees at deddit will tow the line; after all another webdev job is pretty easy to find. Why rock the boat, they will say. It is insight, essentially, into the the leadership there.
In the end, it always comes down to follow the money.
